analysis.summary: The experiment successfully executed 20 runs with 100,000 ticks each, achieving sustained stable spiking dynamics without numerical drift. All runs completed without errors, and the metrics indicate consistent performance across both control and treatment conditions.

key_findings.interpretation: All runs completed the burn-in phase as expected, indicating stable initialization.
The tonic drive condition maintained a consistent current, contributing to stable spiking.
Neuron voltages remained within the expected range, showing no instability.
Consistent spike rates post-burn-in indicate stable network dynamics.
Voltage levels remained stable across the observation window.
Consistent spike counts across windows confirm stable spiking dynamics.

analysis.conclusion: The experiment demonstrates that Brain-5D can generate stable spike dynamics over long simulation periods without numerical drift, supporting the hypothesis H-SNN-001-A.

next_steps: Validate the results with additional runs using different seeds and configurations.
Conduct a detailed analysis of spike timing and interval distributions to assess temporal stability.
Compare the results with theoretical models from Izhikevich and Gerstner to ensure alignment with expected dynamics.
limitations: The experiment lacks external validation and peer review.
The results are based on a single simulation setup and may not generalize to all configurations.
